content: The bravest sight in the world is to see a great man struggling against adversity.
author: Seneca
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Courage is rarely the thunderous heroics we see in movies; it is the quiet voice at the end of the day that says, 'I will try again tomorrow.' When we wait to feel completely fearless before taking a step, we stay trapped in place.

In Seneca's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Real strength shows up with a racing pulse and trembling hands. It is the willingness to be vulnerable, to risk looking foolish, and to stand up for what matters even when everything in you wants to hide.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
